cases.name: A1a the original operation still answers after a newer runtime is activated
A1b quiescence is scoped per target while the operation runs
A2a the terminal state is truthful and the external effect happened exactly once
A2b the target is quiescent once the operation releases ownership
R1 the V1 release becomes collectible once no lease retains it
A3a a failing operation reports Failed, not silence
A3b a cancelled operation reports Cancelled, not silence
A3c neither the failure nor the cancellation added an external effect
A4a an operation lost with its process reports Unknown, with its target preserved
A4b an identifier that was never issued is still reported as NotFound
A4c the recovered host surfaces the lost operation rather than reporting a clean slate
A5a control: reading quiescence does not hold it — work starts in the check-then-act gap

detail.note: a swap acting on the earlier read would destroy work that began after it

cases.name: A5b a swap window is refused while the target has work in flight
A5c holding a swap window closes the gap for its scope and leaves other targets alone
A5d the scope accepts real work again once the window is released
A5e a target window is refused while a global window is held
A5f a global window is refused while a target window is held
A5g the terminal record is already on disk when a window is granted
A5h under contention, no operation is ever admitted for a scope whose window is held
A5i mutation control: the same regression detects a deliberately split admission

detail.note: non-zero here is the point: it shows A5h can fail

cases.name: C1 control: a host with no evidence answers NotFound for the very same lost operation

detail.note: this is the clio 8 behaviour the experiment exists to replace

cases.name: C2 control: the release is retained while its operation runs, and only then collectible
N1 a pre-existing artefact makes presence a FALSE positive for attribution

detail.note: the artefact was written before the operation started and the operation was killed

cases.name: N2 a partially completed operation makes presence a FALSE positive
N3 an intervening operation makes a last-result read answer about the wrong one

detail.note: attributing the last result to the interrupted operation would report v2's outcome as v1's

cases.name: P1 a failed evidence write does NOT rewrite the execution outcome

detail.note: the work succeeded; only its record failed to persist

cases.name: P2 the scope is visibly degraded and automatic retirement is refused

detail.note: refusal is conservative POLICY, not a consequence of the evidence living in the runtime - see P3

cases.name: P3 retiring the runtime does not destroy degraded evidence; only replacing its owner would

detail.note: OperationRecord is a host-contract type held in a host collection, so it survives the release that produced it

cases.name: P4 a failed admission write starts no work and leaves no unfinishable owner

detail.note: evidence is written before registration, so nothing is registered when it fails

cases.name: P5 retirement is refused while owned cleanup is held, and allowed once ownership is released

detail.note: the outcome was Succeeded throughout; only ownership changed

cases.name: L1 a concurrent disposal cannot release ownership before the outcome is recorded

detail.note: Dispose blocks on the lease gate until the in-flight completion has recorded its outcome

cases.name: L2 a rejected completion does not burn the report; the operation can still finish

detail.note: validation happens before the single report is consumed

cases.name: M1 mutation control: the same check detects a lease that reports its flag before the outcome

detail.note: Running here is the defect: ownership was released while the outcome was still unrecorded

cases.name: M2 a torn terminal write keeps the outcome in memory and is never recovered as terminal

detail.note: the half-written line is skipped, so recovery sees begin-without-end

cases.name: M3 a degraded outcome is tracked as un-persisted, not merely as a degraded scope
E3 an un-persisted outcome does NOT survive replacement of the evidence owner

detail.note: clearing a flag would not have changed this — the record was never on disk

cases.name: E4 repair is what makes an outcome durable; removing the fault alone changes nothing

detail.note: the record written is the original outcome, once; nothing is re-executed

cases.name: E5 repair after a torn write survives restart readback

detail.note: the half-line stays on disk and is skipped; the repaired line is the one that reads back

cases.name: E6 with the fault still present, repair fails and explicit loss is the only way forward

detail.note: the outcome is gone and later readers are told Unknown rather than a guess

cases.name: M4 an update that cannot take its window defers, leaving the work untouched

detail.note: deferred rather than applied; no implicit kill, and the work completed normally

cases.name: D1 disproof: polling for an idle moment starves against a continuously busy scope

detail.note: this is the case that would overturn 'defer, never kill' — deferral that never ends

cases.name: D2 reserving first and draining second ends the wait under the same load

detail.note: new admissions are refused under the reservation, so in-flight work is finite

cases.name: E1 a bounded drain over hung work expires instead of holding the scope shut

detail.note: the hung operation was neither killed nor completed; the update defers again

cases.name: E2 admissions reopen once the reservation expires, with the hung work still untouched

detail.note: no implicit kill and no replay; the scope is usable again

cases.name: O1 a runtime-defined result held by the caller keeps the release alive after the operation ended

detail.note: the ledger reported a terminal state and released its own retention; the escaped value did not

cases.name: G1 a runtime-defined exception retains its release exactly like a returned value does

detail.note: an escaping exception is a returned value with extra steps

cases.name: G2 the portable error form lets the release go while the information survives

detail.note: same failure, expressed as strings; nothing retains the release

cases.name: G3 a host progress delegate is not retained by the release after the call

detail.note: the mirror case: a retained host delegate would tie the host graph to the release

cases.name: G4 negative control: a runtime-defined callback keeps the release alive until dropped

detail.note: delegates behave exactly as DTOs and exceptions do — the rule is one rule

cases.name: F1 two operations run concurrently, each pinned to the release that admitted it

detail.note: both ids were seen in Running before either finished, so the overlap is measured

cases.name: F2 an incompatible release is rejected before activation without disturbing V1

detail.note: the release is inspected then discarded; the running release is never consulted

cases.name: F3 a partner workflow composes the pinned release and returns portable data only

detail.note: the partner assembly references the contract and no vendor release

cases.name: F4 the shared contract assembly references no CLI or MCP dependency

detail.note: checked on the assembly that actually crosses the boundary, not on the host

cases.name: H1 an operation whose owner process is gone resolves to Unknown, not Running

detail.note: a killed process disposes nothing, so disposal cannot be what ends ownership

cases.name: H2 the Unknown resolution is written to evidence, not only held in memory

detail.note: a resolution only in memory would be lost by the very replacement that caused it

cases.name: H3 an orphaned operation stops blocking quiescence, so a drain can finish

detail.note: the only thing still retaining was the live owner; the orphan released itself

cases.name: H4 negative control: an operation whose owner process is alive is left Running

detail.note: the sweep resolves absence, it does not resolve everything

cases.name: H5 a genuine late outcome supersedes Unknown, but disposal alone does not

detail.note: Unknown is an admission, so knowledge replaces it and a fabricated Failed does not
